items.followUp: Name any three components of a communication system and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of a communication system.
rubric.description: Defines a communication system as a system that sends or exchanges information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it sends, transmits, or exchanges information.

rubric.why: Checks identification and function of the sender.
rubric.description: The sender or source creates and sends the message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the sender/source and stating that it sends the message.

rubric.why: Checks identification and function of the medium.
rubric.description: The medium or channel carries the message between sender and receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the medium/channel and stating that the message travels through it.

rubric.why: Checks identification and function of the receiver.
rubric.description: The receiver or destination receives the message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the receiver/destination and stating that it receives the message.

modelAnswer: A communication system is a system that sends or exchanges information between two or more entities.
Sender: the source that creates and sends the message.
Medium: the channel through which the message travels.
Receiver: the destination that receives the message.

items.followUp: What is a phishing attack? Give two ways to identify a phishing email.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and purpose of phishing.
rubric.description: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to impersonate a trusted source and trick users into revealing sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing deception or impersonation intended to obtain sensitive information.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of urgency or pressure as a phishing-email characteristic.
rubric.description: A phishing email may use urgent or threatening language to pressure the recipient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying urgent or threatening language or pressure.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of suspicious links or attachments.
rubric.description: A phishing email may contain suspicious links or attachments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying suspicious links, fake links, or attachments.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of requests for confidential information.
rubric.description: A phishing email may ask for passwords, financial details, or other personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a request for passwords or other sensitive personal or financial information.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a fraudulent attempt to impersonate a trusted person or organisation and trick users into revealing sensitive information.
A phishing email may use urgent or threatening language to pressure the recipient.
It may contain suspicious links or attachments.
It may ask the recipient for passwords, financial details, or other personal information.

items.followUp: What does the problem-solving strategy “break it down” mean?

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the Act It Out strategy.
rubric.description: The situation or steps of a problem are physically performed or represented.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem or its steps are acted out or represented.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of the strategy.
rubric.description: Acting out helps make a problem easier to understand and solve.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acting it out helps with understanding or solving the problem.

modelAnswer: Act It Out is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation or steps of a problem are physically performed or represented.
It helps make the problem easier to understand and solve.
